subject: Onsite hardware survey request — GenomicEdge private deployment qualification
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Taylor <ava.taylor@genomicedge.com>, Ben Cho <ben.cho@genomicedge.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy discovery call — on-prem / air-gapped follow-up

Thanks again for the time on today's call — good to meet the GenomicEdge infra team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items related to a private, on-prem (air-gapped) deployment: 

Summary (from our discovery)
- Deployment mode: Private (on-prem, air-gapped) preference. Hosted API is not an option due to patient-data residency.
- Desired timeline: pilot in Q1 2027, production thereafter; procurement lead times are a gating factor.
- Expected footprint: initially 4 x GPU nodes (NVIDIA H100-class preference) with room to expand to 12 nodes over 12 months.
- Compliance/controls: SOC2 + local encryption-at-rest with HSM/KMS integration required.
- Ops model: GenomicEdge ops will handle physical maintenance. Redwood to provide offline upgrade playbook and tooling.

Open technical questions (please confirm):
1) Rack space / power: do you have a preferred rack U-per-node and measured PDU capacity per rack? (see attached site inventory template)
2) Network: will the cluster be fully air-gapped with no outbound egress, or do you allow a restricted egress tunnel for package validation and telemetry via a proxy?
3) Patch windows: typical maintenance windows and allowed blackout periods for upgrades/firmware?
4) Spare parts & support: do you have on-site spares or would you like Redwood to quote a spare-kit?
5) Encryption & key management: preferred HSM vendor and any required certs for integration?

Attachments: site_inventory_template.xlsx (please fill and return), redwood-offline-upgrade-playbook.pdf (reference).

Proposed next steps:
- GenomicEdge to complete the site inventory and return by 2026-10-15.
- Schedule a 45-minute hardware survey call week of 2026-10-19 — Sofia/Rishi + GenomicEdge infra.
- Redwood will prepare an NDA-safe dry-run of the offline upgrade playbook and a preliminary BOM/quote.

If that aligns, Ben/Ava: please confirm the earliest date for the hardware survey and who on your side will own the inventory sheet.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deploy discovery call — on-prem / air-gapped follow-up

Thanks, Sofia — that recap is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Rack / power: each node will be in a 42U rack; planned deployment is 1 node per 4U initially. Our data center provides dual 30A PDUs per rack, but we need to confirm available breaker headroom (I will send measured numbers).
- Network: our security policy requires no persistent outbound egress from the air-gapped VLAN. We can provision a temporary, supervised egress proxy for onboarding and periodic validations if Redwood requires it — we'd need to scope exactly what gets validated.
- Patch windows: production blackout is Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00 local; we prefer upgrades in a weekend maintenance window or after-hours.
- Spares: we keep a minimal spare inventory (1 GPU spare, general spare drives). We may ask Redwood to quote a 2-node spare kit.
- KMS: we use a Thales HSM (nShield). We will share certs under an SRA/secure transfer.

We should be able to return the inventory sheet by 2026-10-16. For the hardware survey, the earliest we can do is 2026-10-22 (US/PST). Ben will own the sheet internally.

Ava Taylor
Head of Infrastructure | GenomicEdge, Inc.

Quick technical follow-ups from our side before the hardware survey so we can prepare the right checklist: 

1) Node sizing: when you say H100-class preference, can you confirm desired GPU memory (80GB v 94GB options) and NVMe local scratch per node (1 TB vs 4 TB)? This affects rack U and power draw estimates.
2) Cooling: does the data center provide cold-aisle containment? We need the ambient inlet temp and whether you have a liquid-cooled option for higher density.
3) OS / image provisioning: do you plan to allow us to bring a pre-baked OS image on USB for offline install, or do you require an image built by your ops team?
4) Network connectivity for KV cache sync/backups: even if fully air-gapped, do you have an internal isolated network segment we can use for model shard syncs, or will all artifacts be transferred manually?

Action: Sofia — if GenomicEdge can provide the measured PDU headroom and estimated inlet temps we can produce a detailed per-node power/cooling worksheet to bring on the call.

Thanks,
Rishi
